reason: As written the test does not discriminate. (1) No null arm: 'residual d_F drops by >=1' is confounded because fixing even 10% of 2l<=14 bits (1-2 vars) lowers d_F for ANY choice, and a WRONG decimation makes the residual UNSAT (refuted at low degree), a spurious drop. No oracle-decimation or random-decimation control is specified; ffd_semaev_core.random_matched exists but is not used. (2) m=2 is the wrong cell: the open lever is d_F growth at m>=3 (cells (4,4..6) unmeasured); at m=2 n=17-21 d_F is a small near-constant so 'drop by 1' is inside noise, and the system has only 2l<=21 unknowns so exact enumeration (2^21 numpy) gives exact marginals; BP is then a strictly dominated heuristic and the only informative output is BP-vs-exact marginal agreement, which the design does not record. (3) Random targets are mostly UNSAT for l<=n/3 (decomposition prob ~2^(2l-n)), where marginals/decimation have no planted truth; BP may not converge. (4) Prediction_if_true compares bias on planted bits at l<=n/3, but at 2l<n equations exceed unknowns (overdetermined, unique solution) so exact marginals are 0/1 - 'bias>0.6' is trivially achievable by an oracle and says nothing about BP. (5) Scaling: three n values 17,19,21 with 2l<=21 give no trend; nothing connects to n=131 unless a size-extrapolable quantity (mean |bias| and BP-exact marginal correlation vs n at fixed l/n, fraction of converged runs) is reported. (6) Metric: msolve F4 max degree from -v 2 table is structural (OK); wall time must not be used. Runtime: 200 inst x 3 n x ~5 l x 2 targets x 2 arms ~ 6000 msolve calls ~ 40+ CPU-min, over the 20-min cap; BP itself is cheap (factor tables 2^(2l) x n eqs). Idea is expected accounting (dense quadratic XOR-like factors, paramagnetic), so the experiment is cheap to run and its likely outcome (marginals ~0.5, BP~exact-uncorrelated) is a clean closure of BP decimation if controls are added.
fix: Redesign: (A) Cells: m=2 as sanity plus m=3 (S_4, 3l unknowns) at n in {15,17,19,21}, l with ml in [n/2.. n] covering both determined and overdetermined; generate instances via ffd_semaev_core.build_system / `ic corpus` .anf; planted target (SAT) only for the decimation test, random target only to report fraction SAT and BP convergence. (B) Ground truth: for ml<=21 compute EXACT marginals by numpy enumeration of all 2^(ml) assignments; primary statistic = Pearson/AUC of BP marginal vs exact marginal and mean |bias-0.5| of BP vs exact; null arms: (i) BP on random_matched system (same degree/density, random coefficients), (ii) BP with shuffled message init, (iii) uniform random 'bias' ranking. Report fraction of runs where BP converged (damping 0.5, 200 its, 3 random inits) and Bethe free energy vs exact log #solutions (log2 count of solutions by enumeration) to test the 'cavity entropy predicts phase' claim, tabulated vs n at fixed l/n. (C) Decimation test with 4 arms on identical instances: BP-top-10% (k=ceil(0.1*ml) vars fixed to BP-argmax), oracle (k vars of the planted solution, same k, chosen at random), random-value (k random vars, random values), none. Record: fraction of BP-fixed bits agreeing with planted (the real decimation accuracy; if <~0.5+eps, closes), residual consistency flag, and msolve -v 2 max F4 deg (and hky_last_fall_degree d_last on the same cell if usable) on residual. Count only consistent residuals when comparing d_F, and report the paired difference vs the oracle arm; a drop counts only if BP arm drop > random-decimation arm drop with CI excluding 0 (paired bootstrap). Include guess cost: expected 2^(#wrong fixed bits) multiplier, so the net metric is log2(cost) = F4 matrix size(rows x cols from msolve table) + #wrong. (D) Budget: 40 instances/cell, 8 cells per m, msolve only on arms with consistent residual; est 3-8 CPU-min BP+enumeration, <=10 min msolve. (E) Scaling clause: pre-register the extrapolable quantities (BP-exact correlation, mean BP bias, accuracy of decimated bits, convergence rate, Bethe-vs-exact entropy gap) and their slope in n at fixed l/n; claim nothing about n=131 beyond 'accounting: poly decimation lowers D polynomially at fixed B=2^l' unless accuracy of BP-fixed bits stays >0.9 with non-decreasing slope in n. Classify as accounting; no security claim.
